rationale: The hypothesis posits that persistent fetal fingertip pads (HP:0001212) and lower eyelid eversion (HP:0000656) have a true prevalence of 0% in KDM6B-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Stolerman syndrome) and that their presence definitively rules out Stolerman syndrome in favor of Kabuki syndrome. However, literature examining histone methylation disorders and chromatin-modifier syndromes explicitly highlights phenotypic overlap between Kabuki syndrome (associated with KDM6A/KMT2D) and KDM6B-related neurodevelopmental disorders, specifically referencing shared dysmorphic features such as eversion of the lateral lower eyelid and digital anomalies including persistent fetal fingertip pads. Furthermore, an assertion of '0% prevalence' based on unassessed cohorts is methodologically invalid, and the documented clinical overlap directly contradicts using these features as absolute exclusionary criteria.

evidence.text: Reviews of histone methylation disorders identify substantial phenotypic overlap between Kabuki syndrome and Stolerman neurodevelopmental syndrome caused by monoallelic pathogenic variants in KDM6B, specifically discussing features such as eversion of the lateral third of the lower eyelid.
